Multispecies coalescent modelling After review of the different trees constructed for the eight partitioning schemes using ML and BI methods, as well as concordance factors, it was apparent that there was phylogenetic discordance in shallower lineages of our dataset, which can be ascribed to gene tree conflicts affecting species tree inference. This incomplete lineage sorting made it necessary to utilise multispecies coalescent modelling to estimate the effects of gene-tree conflict on species-tree inference. This protocol explains how to employ the summary method, Accurate Species TRee ALgorithm (ASTRAL v.5.6.3) [49], and the site-based method, SVDQuartets [50], in PAUP* v4.0a 169 [51]. ASTRAL seeks to find the tree that maximises the number of induced quartet trees in gene trees that are shared by the species tree using pre-estimated gene trees [49], whereas SVDQuartets directly infers the species tree from sequence alignments using singular value decomposition (SVD) to analyse quartets of taxa one at a time, extracting information from patterns of genetic variation across the genome [71]. Assuming that incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) is the only source of discordance between gene and species trees, the multi-species coalescent model predicts that the likelihood of a gene tree quartet matching the species tree topology is greater than the likelihood of matching the two alternatives. Furthermore, the two alternatives will have comparable frequencies [72,73]. We use our Galeomorphi data files as input for the programs. Substitute with your own data files. steps.title: Retrieve mitogenomes from GenBank
steps.instruction: Collect ingroup and outgroup mitogenome sequences and merge them into a single GenBank file.

substeps.instruction: Copy newly assembled mitogenome files (GenBank full format) into folder `1a_Data`.

Create a text file `genbank.list` containing accession numbers of representative ingroup taxa (species/genus/family/order/superorder) and selected outgroups (four Lamniformes and four Orectolobiformes).
Upload `genbank.list` to NCBI Batch Entrez (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/batchentrez) and retrieve the corresponding records from the Nucleotide database.
Select all retrieved records, ensure each is a complete mitogenome, and save them as a single GenBank‑full file.
Merge the downloaded GenBank file with the five newly assembled mitogenomes using the command `cat *.gb > winn_2023.gb`.

steps.title: Extract rRNA and CDS with GBSEQEXTRACTOR
steps.instruction: Use GBSEQEXTRACTOR to pull out rRNA and coding sequences from the merged GenBank file.

substeps.instruction: Download GBSEQEXTRACTOR (see Software and Datasets section) and place it together with `winn_2023.gb` in a new folder `1b_GeneExtract`.
Open a terminal, navigate to `1b_GeneExtract` (`cd ./1b_GeneExtract`).
Run `gbseqextractor -f winn_2023.gb -prefix winn_2023 -types rRNA -s` to create `winn_2023.rrna.fasta`.
Run `gbseqextractor -f winn_2023.gb -prefix winn_2023 -types CDS -s` to create `winn_2023.cds.fasta`.
Concatenate the two fasta files: `cat winn_2023.rrna.fasta winn_2023.cds.fasta > winn_2023.cds-rrna.fasta`.

Open `winn_2023.cds-rrna.fasta` in a text editor and standardise gene names to the following codes: ATP6, ATP8, COX1, COX2, COX3, CYTB, ND1, ND2, ND3, ND4, ND4L, ND5, ND6, 12SrRNA, 16SrRNA. Save as `winn_2023.cds-rrna.std.fasta`.
Extract each gene into its own fasta file using the script `maduna2022-gene-extractions.sh` (see script below).
Rename the mistakenly created `ND4;.fa` to `ND4.fa` and replace any remaining semicolons in filenames with underscores: `for f in *.fa; do sed -i 's/;/_/g' "$f"; done`.

steps.title: Prepare MACSE2 alignment folder
steps.instruction: Set up MACSE2 environment and verify coding‑gene orientation.

substeps.instruction: Create folder `2a_MACSE2` and download the latest MACSE version (`macse_v2.06.jar`).
Upload the extracted protein‑coding genes (PCGs) from `1b_GeneExtract` into Geneious.
Check each PCG orientation: all should be 5′→3′ except ND6, which must be reverse‑complemented (Sequence → Reverse complement… → Reverse complement entire sequence) and saved as `ND6_rev_comp.fa`.
Save all correctly oriented PCG fasta files into `2a_MACSE2`.

steps.title: Align PCGs with MACSE2
steps.instruction: Run MACSE2 on each protein‑coding gene to produce codon‑aware nucleotide alignments.

substeps.instruction: Create a variable `datadir=./2a_MACSE2`.
Execute the following loop:
`for i in $datadir/*.fa; do java -jar -Xmx600m macse_v2.06.jar -prog alignSequences -seq "$i" -gc_def 2; done`
Note: `-gc_def 2` specifies the Vertebrate Mitochondrial genetic code (code 2).

steps.title: Align rRNAs with MAFFT online
steps.instruction: Generate rRNA alignments using the MAFFT Q‑INS‑i algorithm.

substeps.instruction: Open the MAFFT web server (https://mafft.cbrc.jp/alignment/server/index.html).
Upload each rRNA fasta file extracted in step 2.
Select the Q‑INS‑i iterative refinement method, set the direction according to the first sequence (5′→3′), and leave all other parameters at default.
Run the alignment and download the resulting fasta files.

steps.title: Clean alignments in Geneious and BMGE
steps.instruction: Remove stop codons, ensure frame consistency, and filter ambiguous sites.

substeps.instruction: Open all PCG alignments from `2a_MACSE2` in Geneious.
Set translation table to Vertebrate Mitochondrial (transl_table 2).
Delete any stop codons; keep start codons (e.g., ATG, GTG).
Confirm each alignment length is divisible by 3.
Open each rRNA alignment in Geneious and repeat the above cleaning steps.
Run BMGE (v1.12_1) on each PCG and rRNA alignment with default settings (DNA mode, sequence coding).
Export the cleaned alignments to folder `2c_CleanEdit`.

steps.title: Concatenate alignments and create datasets
steps.instruction: Combine gene alignments into concatenated supermatrices and generate summary files.

substeps.instruction: Import all cleaned alignments from `2c_CleanEdit` back into Geneious.
Sort each alignment by name (right‑click → Sort → By Name).

Select the 13 PCG alignments, then use Tools → Concatenate Sequences or Alignments → Concatenate. Save as `Galeomorphii_13PCGs_NT` in FASTA, NEXUS, and PHYLIP formats inside folder `2d_ConCat` (Dataset 1).
Select the 13 PCGs plus the two rRNA alignments, concatenate, and save as `Galeomorphii_13PCGs_2rRNAs_NT` (Dataset 2) in the same three formats.
Translate the nucleotide PCG concatenation (`Galeomorphii_13PCGs_NT`) to amino‑acid sequences using Geneious and save as `Galeomorphii_13PCGs_AA` (Dataset 3) in FASTA, NEXUS, and PHYLIP.
Generate length‑summary tables (gene length and alignment positions) from Geneious alignment information for use in downstream partition files.

steps.title: Assess substitution saturation with DAMME
steps.instruction: Perform two‑tailed saturation tests for each codon position and for whole datasets.

substeps.instruction: Copy all cleaned gene alignments (FASTA) from `2c_CleanEdit` and the concatenated files from `2d_ConCat` into a new folder `3_DAMBE`.
Open DAMBE, choose File → Open standard sequence file, select "Protein‑coding Nuc. Seq." for PCGs (genetic code 2) and "Non‑Protein Nuc. Seq." for rRNAs.
For each dataset, run "Sequences → Work on codon positions 1 and 2" (repeat for positions 1, 3, 1+2, and all positions).

Estimate proportion of invariant sites (P(inv)) via Seq. Analysis → Substitution rates over sites → Estimate proportion of invariant sites, using the Neighbour‑Joining tree building option (default settings). Record the reported P(inv) (e.g., 0.18763).

Run substitution‑saturation test (Seq. Analysis → Measure Substitution Saturation → Test by Xia et al.) entering the obtained P(inv) value and click Go!. Record Iss and critical Iss values for both symmetrical and asymmetrical topologies.

steps.title: Chi‑square test and concordance factor plots (Lanfear R script)
steps.instruction: Test differences between gene‑tree and site‑tree support and visualise results.

substeps.instruction: Install required R packages: `viridis`, `ggplot2`, `dplyr`, `ggrepel`, `GGally`, `entropy`.
Read the concordance‑factor statistics file (e.g., `PS05_run03_concord.cf.stat`) with `read.delim`. Rename columns 18 and 19 to `bootstrap` and `branchlength`.
Compute χ² p‑values for gene‑CF and site‑CF using `chisq(gDF1, gDF2, gN)` and `chisq(sDF1, sDF2, sN)`. Store as `gEF_p` and `sEF_p`.
Calculate entropy‑based metrics (`ENT`, `ENTC`) for each partition.
Create a PDF of the relationship between gCF, sCF, and bootstrap values (Figure 9) using `ggpairs`.
Create a PDF of internode certainty (Figure 10) with `ggpairs` on the same data.
Save both PDFs.

steps.title: Visualise ML, BI, and concordance trees in FigTree
steps.instruction: Root, colour, and annotate trees for presentation.

substeps.instruction: Open all `.nex.tree` files from maximum‑likelihood (ML) and Bayesian‑inference (BI) analyses in FigTree.
Root each tree using the designated outgroup.
Align nodes in increasing order, colour branches/nodes of interest (e.g., colour Triakidae pink).
Display bootstrap values, concordance factors, and posterior probabilities on the tree.
Export each annotated tree as a PNG file (Figures 11‑13).

steps.title: ASTRAL species‑tree inference
steps.instruction: Generate gene trees, combine them, and run ASTRAL with various options.

substeps.instruction: For each of the 13 PCGs and 2 rRNAs, run IQ‑Tree on the cleaned single‑gene alignments:
`for gene in *.fas; do iqtree2 -s $gene -st DNA -m MFP -AICc -nt AUTO -B 1000; done`
Concatenate all resulting `.treefile` files: `cat *.treefile > Galeomorphi.15gene.tre`.
Convert the combined treefile to Newick format (e.g., `Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G.tre`).
Run ASTRAL (default options): `java -jar astral.5.7.8.jar -i Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G.tre -o Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-ASTRAL.tre`.
Annotate branches (see ASTRAL tutorial) – example command:
`java -jar astral.5.7.8.jar -q Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-ASTRAL.tre -i Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G.tre -t 2 -o Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-scored-t2.tre`
Collapse low‑support branches using Newick Utilities:
`nw_ed Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G.tre 'i & b Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-BS10.tre'`
Re‑run ASTRAL on the collapsed treeset:
`java -jar astral.5.7.8.jar -i Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-BS10.tre -o Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-BS10-ASTRAL.tre`
Generate posterior probabilities for the main topology and the two alternatives:
`java -jar astral.5.7.8.jar -q Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-ASTRAL.tre -i Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G.tre -t 4 -o Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-scored-t4.tre`
Show quartet support for main and alternative topologies:
`java -jar astral.5.7.8.jar -q Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-ASTRAL.tre -i Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G.tre -t 8 -o Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-scored-t8.tre`
Test for polytomies (Sayyari & Mirarab 2018) using the χ²‑based command:
`java -jar astral.5.7.8.jar -q Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-ASTRAL.tre -i Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G.tre -t 10 -o Galeomorphii-mitophy-15G-scored-t10.tre`
Visualise all ASTRAL trees in FigTree or Evolview.

steps.title: SVDQuartets species‑tree inference
steps.instruction: Run SVDQuartets in PAUP* using a nexus file with gene partitions.

substeps.instruction: Create a Nexus file containing the 13 PCG + 2 rRNA alignment (`Data_23_13PCGs_2rRNAs_NT_svd_partitions`).
Open the Nexus file in PAUP* (v4.0a169).
Select the multispecies coalescent model, set random quartet sampling to 100,000 replicates and bootstrap replicates to 1,000 (all other parameters default).
Execute SVDQuartets and save the bootstrap consensus tree as a PNG image.

steps.title: Test compositional heterogeneity with AliGROOVE
steps.instruction: Run AliGROOVE on nucleotide and amino‑acid datasets with and without treating indels as ambiguous.

substeps.instruction: Set `aligroove=./bin/AliGROOVE` (path to the executable).
Run without `-N` (indels as fifth character):
`$aligroove/AliGROOVE_v.1.08.pl -i Data_14_Galeomorphii_13PCGs_NT.fasta`
`$aligroove/AliGROOVE_v.1.08.pl -i Data_17_Galeomorphii_13PCGs_2rRNAs_NT.fasta`
`$aligroove/AliGROOVE_v.1.08.pl -i Data_20_Galeomorphii_13PCGs_AA.fasta`
Run with `-N` (indels ambiguous) for the two nucleotide datasets:
`$aligroove/AliGROOVE_v.1.08.pl -N -i Data_14_Galeomorphii_13PCGs_NT.fasta`
`$aligroove/AliGROOVE_v.1.08.pl -N -i Data_17_Galeomorphii_13PCGs_2rRNAs_NT.fasta`

steps.title: Assess base‑composition bias with BaCoCa
steps.instruction: Execute BaCoCa to generate heat‑maps and heterogeneity statistics.

substeps.instruction: Set `bacoca=./BaCoCa_v1.1_Skript_Perl`.
Run BaCoCa with default settings and the `-r` option to produce heat‑maps:
`perl $bacoca/BaCoCa.v1.109.r.pl -i 13PCGs_2rRNAs_NT.fasta -P 13PCGs_2rRNAs_NT.part.txt -r`

steps.title: Run PHYLOBAYES_MPI Bayesian analyses
steps.instruction: Perform MCMC runs for four models (GTR+G4, CAT‑Poisson+G4, CAT‑GTR+G4, C60‑GTR+G4) on three datasets.

substeps.instruction: Define paths: `phylobayes=./data` and `mod_sel=./scripts`.
For each dataset, launch two independent chains per model using `mpirun -np <cores> $phylobayes/pb_mpi` with the appropriate flags (see commands below).
Example for GTR on Dataset 1 (13PCGs_NT):
`mpirun -np 8 $phylobayes/pb_mpi -ncat 1 -gtr -d Data_15_Galeomorphii_13PCGs_NT.phy GTR_13PCGs_NT_chain1 &`
`mpirun -np 8 $phylobayes/pb_mpi -ncat 1 -gtr -d Data_15_Galeomorphii_13PCGs_NT.phy GTR_13PCGs_NT_chain2 &`

Repeat analogous commands for Dataset 2 (13PCGs_2rRNAs_NT) and Dataset 3 (13PCGs_AA) and for the three other models (CAT‑Poisson, CAT‑GTR, C60‑GTR) using the flag combinations shown in the original protocol.
After each pair of chains finishes, assess convergence:
`$phylobayes/tracecomp GTR_13PCGs_NT_chain?.trace -o GTR_13PCGs_NT_tracecomp`
`$phylobayes/bpcomp -x <burnin> 10 GTR_13PCGs_NT_chain1 GTR_13PCGs_NT_chain2 -o GTR_13PCGs_NT_bpcomp`
Use a 20 % burn‑in for all bpcomp/tracecomp analyses.
Check convergence in Tracer (v1.7.1) – look for maxdiff < 0.1, ESS > 100, rel_diff < 0.1.
Generate site‑specific log‑likelihoods with `readpb_mpi` (example for GTR Dataset 1):
`mpirun -np 48 $phylobayes/readpb_mpi -x 813 32 -sitelogl GTR_13PCGs_NT_chain1`
`mpirun -np 48 $phylobayes/readpb_mpi -x 813 32 -sitelogl GTR_13PCGs_NT_chain2`
Repeat `readpb_mpi` for all models and datasets using the `-x` and `-sitelogl` parameters listed in the protocol.
Collect site‑specific scores:
`python3 ../scripts/read_loocv_waic.py GTR_13PCGs_NT_chain?.sitelogl`
`python3 ../scripts/read_loocv_waic.py CAT-POISSON_13PCGs_NT_chain?.sitelogl`
`python3 ../scripts/read_loocv_waic.py CAT-GTR_13PCGs_NT_chain?.sitelogl`
`python3 ../scripts/read_loocv_waic.py C60-GTR_AA_chain?.sitelogl`
Compute wAIC and LOO‑CV statistics using the provided `read_loocv_waic.py` script (see R code snippet in the protocol).
Summarise convergence statistics and model‑comparison scores in a table (as in Table 7 of the original protocol).

steps.title: Visualise Bayesian trees and compare models
steps.instruction: Load each posterior tree into FigTree, annotate, and generate summary figures.

substeps.instruction: Open the consensus trees for each model/dataset in FigTree.
Display posterior probabilities at nodes.
Export each visualisation as a PNG (e.g., Figure 21).

description: Validation of protocol This full protocol has been used and validated in the following research article: • Winn et al. [83]. A comprehensive phylogenomic study unveils evolutionary patterns and challenges in the mitochondrial genomes of Carcharhiniformes: A focus on Triakidae. Genomics . 116(1): 110771. doi: 10.1016/j.ygeno.2023.110771 An extensive statistical workflow was used to expand the phylogeny of Triakidae. We began by retrieving representative mitogenomes from the Carcharhiniform order, including four outgroups each from the Lamniform and Orectolobiform orders, and merged the GenBank records with our newly assembled mitogenomes as per the sequence alignment and concatenation pipeline of Section A (these mitogenomes are available as Data 13 on Dryad). Hereafter, we extracted protein-coding genes (PCGs) and ribosomal (r)RNAs, manually standardised gene names, extracted and orientated individual genes in the correct order, produced codon-aware multiple sequence alignments for each of the 13 PCGs using MACSE and the rRNAs using MAFFT with the Q-INS-i algorithm, manually trimmed the alignments in Geneious, and removed any remaining ambiguously aligned sites using BMGE. The gene alignments were used to produce three concatenated mitogenomic datasets: Dataset 1: 13PCGs_NT dataset; Dataset 2: 13PCGs_rRNAs_NT; Dataset 3: 13PCGs_AA dataset (available as Data 14–23 on Dryad). Length summaries were saved to use for partition file construction. In Section B, we performed two-tailed tests of substitution saturation [56] for each gene and each codon position of the 13PCGs as well as on the entire 13PCGs_NT and 13PCGs_rRNAs_NT datasets in DAMBE [42,43]. We also plotted the number of transitions (s) and transversions (v) vs. divergence to visually inspect substitution saturation.
